//: ChessIQ Realtime Database rules.
Deploy with:  firebase deploy --only database
These rules cover the Ranked nodes added in v1.6. The pre-existing /users
and /positions rules are reproduced here to match current behaviour so
deploying this file does not silently change the casual app.
KNOWN ISSUE, not fixed here: /users is readable by any authenticated user
because leaderboard.html, admin-dashboard.js and the Ranked rank lookup all
read the whole node, and /users/{uid}/email holds a real address. Closing
that needs the email field relocated to /private and a /leaderboard
projection built first. Tracked as item 1 of the pre-Ranked list.
A sender writes exactly one node here, keyed by their own uid,
so a request can never be forged as coming from someone else.
Deleting is left to the recipient, who already has write access
through the parent rule.

out.//: Cleared by the other side when they accept or decline.

//: Writable by the friend only while a request between the two
actually exists, which is what makes accept able to write both
sides at once. Removal is allowed either way so unfriending
does not leave a dangling half.
NOTE: .write cascades, so the owner can already write here via
the $uid rule above. This clause exists to let the OTHER party
complete the handshake, not to restrict the owner.

duelInvites.//: A friend drops a pointer to a duel they just created.

$duelId..write: auth != null && (auth.uid === $uid || (newData.exists() && newData.child('from').val() === auth.uid && root.child('users/' + $uid + '/friends/' + auth.uid).exists()))

//: Readable by any signed-in player because quick match scans the queue
client side to find someone waiting. Each player owns their own entry.
The one exception is matchedDuelId: the player doing the claiming must
be able to stamp it onto the waiting player's entry, which is how
pairing happens without a server. It may only be written when it is
currently empty, so a claim cannot be stolen or overwritten.
Readable while waiting so a challenge link can be opened by someone
who is not yet a participant, and afterwards only by the two players.
Writable by either participant, plus the open-slot case where a
joining player writes themselves in as guest.
$duelId..read: auth != null && (!data.exists() || data.child('status').val() === 'waiting' || data.child('host/uid').val() === auth.uid || data.child('guest/uid').val() === auth.uid)
$duelId..write: auth != null && (!data.exists() || data.child('host/uid').val() === auth.uid || data.child('guest/uid').val() === auth.uid || (data.child('status').val() === 'waiting' && !data.child('guest').exists() && newData.child('guest/uid').val() === auth.uid) || newData.child('host/uid').val() === auth.uid)

//: NOTE: .write cascades in RTDB, so the $duelId rule above already
grants both participants write access here and this rule cannot
revoke it. Duel scores are therefore client-authoritative in
v1.0 — the .validate bounds below are the real guard, and they
only cap the range, not the honesty. A determined player can
write themselves a 1500. Closing that needs a Cloud Function to
own settlement; acceptable for link-based duels among friends,
not for a public competitive ladder.

result.//: Settled by whichever client observes both players finished.
